problem_summary.summary: Choose k distinct values from 1 through n and return every combination, where order within a combination does not matter.
problem_summary.input_output: Inputs: n and k. Return all size-k subsets of the integers in [1, n].

brute_force.explanation: Enumerate every length-k sequence whose entries come from 1 through n, then keep only sequences that are strictly increasing. This is a direct but highly redundant way to represent unordered choices.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Every valid combination has one increasing sequence representation, and that sequence is among all enumerated length-k sequences. Strictly increasing filtering rejects repeats and all reordered duplicates.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(k * n^k) — enumerate n^k sequences and check each completed sequence; this ignores the additional cost of storing output copies.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(k) auxiliary for the current sequence and recursion, excluding output.

optimized.explanation: Build combinations in increasing order. Once a value is chosen, recurse only with larger values; stop starting branches when too few values remain to reach size k.
optimized.correctness_idea: Increasing choices give each unordered subset exactly one path. The upper bound n - (k - chosen) + 1 ensures every remaining slot can still be filled, so no valid combination is pruned.
optimized.time_complexity: O(k * C(n,k)) — copy each of the C(n,k) result combinations; the search visits only prefixes of valid combinations.
optimized.space_complexity: O(k) auxiliary for the current path and recursion, excluding O(k * C(n,k)) output.

steps.event: Choose 2, then enumerate the final slot.
steps.condition: 2 through 4 can begin a completable pair.
steps.action: For prefix [1,2], try 3, 4, and 5 as final values; record three leaves.
Choose final values 4 and 5; then backtrack.
Record [1,4,5], then return to the root.

steps.condition: Root choices greater than 3 cannot fill three slots.

edge_cases.handling: Each value from 1 through n is returned as a one-element combination.
The bounded loop skips prefixes that cannot be extended to k values.
